_schema: One JSON object per line. Fields: timestamp (ISO 8601), section (NN), paragraph (int, 1-based), claim_text (string, max 200 chars), support_type (evidence-card | footnote | unmapped), support_ref (path to evidence card OR footnote number OR null), reason (string, only present when support_type=unmapped, one of: evidence-gap | not-yet-harvested | requires-primary-source | intentional-conjecture), audited_in_run (int, the run_count when this claim was first audited), confidence (float 0-1, agent's confidence in the mapping). Initial seed entry below; the verify-provenance sub-task appends one entry per claim per section per audit run.

claim_text: The LMS files arrive in a learning-management folder as a flat list organized only by name.
Expert review is built into the process at defined checkpoints where the professor inspects, corrects, and gates whether the work advances.
The case study is a reviewed static website, not a conversational agent or chatbot placed in front of students.
The article makes no claim that students learned more, because it has not run the study that would license such a claim.
The case study became a live knowledge system of 198 pages: 92 case briefs, 27 doctrinal topic pages, and 79 lecture summaries.
The case study is published at https://constitutionallaw.netlify.app and is readable by anyone (URL verified live).
Each case page is written against the indexed judicial opinion rather than a paraphrase, so a quotation traces to the controlling source.
The doctrinal scope is the structural constitution (judicial review, federalism, separation of powers, commerce power, executive authority, justiciability, Reconstruction amendments).
note: mapped but scope characterization inconsistent with Section IV.A; see PI-118

claim_text: The deployed vault carries a wiki-link grammar linking topics to cases and lectures, cases to topics and citing cases, and lectures to the cases and topics they covered.
Abrams's reframing of the Socratic method belongs to a JLE line of pedagogical-reform pieces that adapt inherited teaching forms rather than rejecting them.
The most recent meta-review of AI in higher education calls for greater ethics, collaboration, and rigour in how such research is conducted and reported.

The deployed case study at https://constitutionallaw.netlify.app presents a fixed shell: top-nav Dashboard/Cases/Topics/Lectures/Recent/About, a brand row 'Con Law I . Prof. Chandler . Spring 2026', and a CMD-K search trigger labeled 'Search cases, topics, doctrines'.
The site has no login, no chat box, no account, and no personalization surface, and every top-nav link routes inside the shell through a hash route rather than a server-rendered page load.

The site carries three discovery surfaces: the Recent tab, the CMD-K palette indexing case names, topic names, doctrine families, and lecture titles, and the four-family Topics grid plus the Cases area filter rail.

claim_text: The Topics index renders a four-family grid keyed to the doctrine_family enum: Federalism, Separation of Powers, Individual Rights, and Justiciability.
The Federalism family card set includes Commerce Clause, Enumerated Powers, and Necessary and Proper Clause.

The Commerce Clause Topic page renders Overview, a Governing Rule block, a Doctrinal Development section, a thirteen-row Key Cases table, a five-by-six comparison matrix on the Wickard-through-NFIB cases, a Hypothetical Applications block, a How-to-Spot-on-an-Exam framework, and a four-paragraph Critique.

The Governing Rule block attaches controlling cases inline: Gibbons v. Ogden (1824), NLRB v. Jones & Laughlin Steel (1937), Wickard v. Filburn (1942), United States v. Lopez (1995), Gonzales v. Raich (2005), and NFIB v. Sebelius (2012).

The Marbury v. Madison (1803) Case brief carries the nine-section case-briefer standard: Memory Jogger, Facts, Procedural History, Judicial Votes, Holding, Analysis, Hypothetical Applications, Critique, and Key Quotations.

The deployed shell renders a structured holding bar from the frontmatter (citation, court, doctrine_family, midpage_id, applied_in), whose applied_in chain names six downstream cases including Martin v. Hunter's Lessee, McCulloch, The Prize Cases, and City of Boerne.
